name: Google Cloud — GenAI Forward Deployed Engineer
jdSummary: Embedded builder-consultant on the Google Cloud Go-To-Market team. Ships bespoke agentic solutions inside the customer's environment: Vertex AI + Gemini, multi-agent (LangGraph / CrewAI / Google ADK), MCP servers, RAG over enterprise data silos, evaluation + observability for accuracy / safety / latency, and converting field signal into product roadmap. Dual-purpose: white-glove deployment + critical feedback loop to engineering. Expects Python / TypeScript fluency and confidence running technical discovery with executives, security, and analysts in the room.
mustHaveSkills: Production-grade Python / TypeScript AI applications
Architecting on Google Cloud (Vertex AI, Gemini, Agent Engine)
Multi-agent systems (LangGraph, CrewAI, Google ADK)
Model Context Protocol (MCP) server design + auth
RAG pipelines over structured + unstructured data; vector DBs (pgvector, Vertex Vector Search)
Evaluation + observability frameworks for agents (faithfulness, trajectory, latency)
Technical discovery sessions with execs, security, and end users
Customer-embedded delivery; turning field pain into product feedback
niceToHaveSkills: LLM-native unit economics (tokens/sec, cost-per-request, cache hit rate)
OpenTelemetry / granular tracing for agent runs
Master's or PhD in AI / CS

revisionLanes.name: 30-min cram
revisionLanes.description: The night before the call: the 8 questions that define the role. Skim these and you can hold a conversation about Vertex grounding, ADK, MCP, multi-agent, LLM cost, and how you run a discovery session.

revisionLanes.name: 1-day deep prep
revisionLanes.description: Full coverage of the JD must-haves: every new GCP/FDE-specific question plus the nearest existing depth on LLM fundamentals, RAG, agents, eval, safety, vectors, and prompt engineering. Aim to answer each in your own words without notes.

revisionLanes.name: 3-day mastery
revisionLanes.description: If the loop is on-site or includes a system-design round: extend the 1-day plan with deeper RAG/agent/safety/foundations material, Python engineering, behavioral STAR, and staff-plus signal questions. Pair with the evaluation criteria and patterns pages.

name: Senior AI/ML Engineer — Azure & Databricks
jdSummary: Senior IC who designs and ships end-to-end ML systems: classical (XGBoost / LightGBM, PyTorch / TensorFlow) plus LLM/GenAI (RAG, fine-tuning, eval, agentic workflows). Owns the full MLOps lifecycle — CI/CD for ML, MLflow tracking + registry, monitoring, drift detection, retraining — on **Azure ML + Databricks** (AWS deliberately out of scope here). Bridges product/engineering/data teams, mentors other engineers, and sets technical standards. Strong opinions on data plane (PySpark, Delta Lake, lakehouse), vector DBs (Pinecone / Weaviate / Milvus / pgvector / Azure AI Search), and LLM evaluation (RAGAS, golden sets).
mustHaveSkills: End-to-end ML systems in production (training → registry → serving → monitoring)
Deep learning (PyTorch primary, TensorFlow when needed) + classical ML (XGBoost / LightGBM)
LLM apps: RAG, fine-tuning (LoRA / PEFT), prompt engineering, eval pipelines (RAGAS)
MLOps: MLflow, CI/CD for ML, model registry, drift detection, retraining triggers
Vector DB selection + hybrid search (Pinecone, Weaviate, Milvus, FAISS, pgvector, Azure AI Search)
Data plane: PySpark, Delta Lake, medallion architecture on Databricks
Azure ML lifecycle: workspaces, compute, endpoints, model monitoring
Feature store design (Feast / Databricks Feature Store) with online + offline parity
Mentorship and platform-level architectural input
niceToHaveSkills: Observability: Evidently AI, Arize, custom drift dashboards

revisionLanes.description: Night before the call. Eight questions that hit the exact shape of the JD: classical vs DL, vector DB selection, LoRA decision, MLflow promotion, drift loop, Azure ML lifecycle, PySpark + Delta, and a behavioral standard-setting story.

revisionLanes.name: 1-day deep prep
revisionLanes.description: Full coverage of every JD must-have: PyTorch internals, classical ML trade-offs, vector DB landscape, LoRA/PEFT recipe, RAGAS eval, MLflow + orchestrators + drift + feature store, Azure ML end-to-end, and PySpark / Delta. Then the nearest existing depth on LLM fundamentals, RAG, evaluation, vectors, safety, and Python.

jdSummary: Senior backend IC building cloud-native services in C# / ASP.NET Core on Azure. Owns API design (APIM), event-driven and serverless workloads (Functions, Logic Apps, Service Bus), containerized services (AKS / Container Apps), identity (managed identity, OAuth/OIDC, Key Vault), and the resilience + observability story. Expected to debug production incidents (async deadlocks, connection-pool exhaustion, latency spikes), apply Well-Architected principles, and mentor on idiomatic async, LINQ, and DI. Strong on system design for regulated, high-availability workloads.

ASP.NET Core APIs + API Management (policies, versioning, throttling)
Event-driven + serverless: Azure Functions, Logic Apps, Service Bus, idempotency, DLQ
Containers: AKS / Container Apps, health probes, autoscaling
Identity: managed identity, OAuth 2.0 / OIDC, JWT validation, Key Vault references
Production debugging: deadlocks, thread-pool starvation, connection pools, GC pressure
System design for HA / multi-region with Well-Architected trade-offs
niceToHaveSkills: EF Core query tuning (deferred execution, N+1 avoidance)

name: RAG & Azure AI Search Specialist
jdSummary: AI engineer specializing in grounded retrieval systems on Azure AI Search and Azure OpenAI. Owns the full RAG pipeline — chunking, embeddings, hybrid (BM25 + vector) retrieval with RRF, reranking, grounding and citations, and production hardening. Builds the evaluation harness (faithfulness, context precision, LLM-as-judge with calibration) and the offline-gate + online-monitoring loop. Hardens against prompt injection and hallucination, tunes vector indexes (HNSW, quantization), and decides when to RAG vs fine-tune.
mustHaveSkills: End-to-end RAG: chunking, embeddings, retrieval, reranking, grounding, citations
Azure AI Search: hybrid search, semantic ranking, RRF fusion
Vector index tuning: HNSW (M/efSearch), quantization, recall/latency trade-offs
RAG evaluation: faithfulness, context precision, golden sets, LLM-as-judge calibration
Offline eval gate + online guardrail monitoring
Prompt-injection and hallucination defenses
RAG vs fine-tune decision framework
niceToHaveSkills: Document Intelligence for ingestion of complex PDFs
